newsitem.title: CANADA: Trade chiefs urge WTO hopefuls to speed up talks.
newsitem.headline: Trade chiefs urge WTO hopefuls to speed up talks.

text.p: The trade ministers from the world's biggest trade partners on Friday urged countries hoping to join the World Trade Organization to move their talks forward as quickly as possible.

"We...confirmed our support for the early accession of applicants on commercially viable terms in a manner that preserves the integrity of WTO rules," ministers from Canada, the United States, the European Union and Japan said in their final communique. "We encourage those acceding to move their negotiations forward as quickly as possible, including on market access for goods and services."
Officials said the bids from China and Russia to join the WTO were at the top of the agenda in talks about expanding the international body.
But China's accession to the WTO would likely depend a lot on politics in the United States, said Karl Falkenberg, a senior negotiator for the European Union.

"The bottom line is going to be how the Congress is going to look at that," since welcoming China into the WTO would in effect give China permanent most-favored-nation status in trade relations with the United States, Falkenberg said in an interview.
The Quad ministers also resolved to move forward with talks on opening up financial services markets.
They agreed to table their requests by mid-June and their offers for liberalization not later than July 14.
